input: Komga on the nas has two libraries, Comics and Manga, and the API shows both configured scanInterval=EVERY_6H, unavailable=False. Comics scans fine every 6 hours. But /volume1/manga holds 279 downloaded chapters (newest .cbz dated Jul 27) and Komga's Manga library still shows just 1 series with 1 book, indexed Jul 23 — nothing new for days. The container log repeats every 6h: "LibraryScanScheduler : Periodic scan for library: Manga" -> "TaskEmitter : Sending task: ScanLibrary(libraryId='0R33RZ4PAF7JC', ...)" -> "TaskHandler : Cannot execute task ScanLibrary(...): Library does not exist". Meanwhile the API lists the Manga library with id 0R3629KVZ4AKY. Our chain checks (suwayomi-feeds-komga, komga-libraries-consumer) are green. What's the root cause, the quickest fix, and why did monitoring miss it?
reference: Verified root cause (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed): Komga's LibraryScanScheduler is firing a STALE libraryId. Id 0R33RZ4PAF7JC belongs to the original pre-read-18 Manga library that was deleted when the library was re-homed to /manga; the scheduler resolved the name 'Manga' but kept emitting ScanLibrary for the deleted id ever since. In 168h of logs: 'Library does not exist' x28, scans of the real id 0R3629KVZ4AKY x0, 'Scanning folder: /manga' x0 — so the real Manga library has NEVER been periodically scanned, leaving 279 chapters (Spy x Family 155, My Dress-Up Darling 124) invisible to readers for 6 days. The scanner itself works (Comics scans on schedule), files exist on disk, and the library config is correct — it is purely the scheduler holding a stale registration. Quickest fixes: restart the Komga container so the scheduler re-registers against current library ids, or trigger a manual scan via POST /api/v1/libraries/0R3629KVZ4AKY/scan (then confirm the new series appear). Monitoring missed it because both chain checks only assert series>=1 — shallow thresholds that the 1 old series satisfies (green-but-broken pattern); a proper check should assert content freshness/count against the filesystem.

checklist.desc: Identifies the root cause: the scan scheduler holds/emits a stale libraryId from an earlier (deleted/recreated) Manga library, so the real library id never gets scanned
Gives a correct quick fix: restart Komga to re-register the scheduler, and/or trigger a manual scan of the real library id via the API (POST /api/v1/libraries/{id}/scan)
Proposes a valid confirmation: grep logs showing zero ScanLibrary/scan-folder events for the real id (vs Comics scanning normally), or compare disk chapter count vs library book count
Explains the monitoring gap: the chain checks only assert series>=1, which the single stale series satisfies — threshold too shallow to catch a frozen library
Rules out scanner/filesystem/config breakage (Comics scans prove the scanner works; files are on disk; library config itself is correct)

input: After the rig came back from a day-long power-off, Suwayomi is acting like it lost everything: inside the container, /home/suwayomi/.local/share/Tachidesk/downloads/ is EMPTY and downloads/thumbnails is 'No such file or directory'; the log has recurring java.io.FileNotFoundException .../thumbnails/<id>.tmp for every manga in the library. But on the rig HOST, /mnt/nas-manga (CIFS mount of the NAS manga share) is healthy and contains mangas/ + thumbnails/, and the DB still says 279 chapters downloaded. docker inspect suwayomi shows StartedAt=2026-08-01T14:25:47Z and both binds with Propagation=rprivate; `systemctl show 'mnt-nas\x2dmanga.mount' -p ActiveEnterTimestamp` says 'Sat 2026-08-01 10:25:52 EDT'. Host timezone is EDT. What happened, what's the risk if I leave it, and what's the immediate + durable fix?

source.ref: record 14 (high, rig/suwayomi docker bind vs CIFS mount)

reference: Verified root cause (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed): a container-vs-mount boot race. Converting timezones, the container started at 10:25:47 EDT (14:25:47Z) — 5 seconds BEFORE the CIFS mount became active at 10:25:52 EDT. With rprivate bind propagation, the bind captured the empty underlying /mnt/nas-manga directory (the pre-mount underlay, root-owned, Jul 23 mtime), and the container never sees the mount that arrived afterwards. Hence: container view empty/ENOENT while host view is healthy; all 279 chapters unservable; ~60 thumbnail FileNotFoundException errors per 96h across 19 manga. Risk if left: any new automatic/manual chapter download writes into the hidden underlay on the rig's root filesystem — silently never reaching /volume1/manga or Komga (and invisible once the mount is up). No data has been lost — the NAS content is intact; the container just cannot see it. The check suwayomi-feeds-komga stayed green because it probes mount writability from the rig HOST, not from inside the container. Immediate fix: restart the suwayomi container (re-creates the bind on top of the live mount). Durable fix: add an ordering/dependency so the container cannot start before the mount (systemd unit ordering/BindsTo on mnt-nas\x2dmanga.mount, or compose dependency), or use rslave/shared bind propagation so a late mount propagates into the container. Regression of read-18 hardening (mount was made persistent+ordered, but the container had no guard).

checklist.desc: Identifies the boot race: the container started seconds BEFORE the CIFS mount became active (correctly reconciling 14:25:47Z = 10:25:47 EDT vs mount 10:25:52 EDT), so the rprivate bind captured the empty pre-mount underlay directory
Immediate fix: restart the suwayomi container so the bind re-captures the now-live mount
Durable fix: enforce start ordering/dependency on the mount unit (systemd/compose) and/or use rslave (shared) bind propagation instead of rprivate
Names the risk of leaving it: new downloads write into the hidden underlay on the rig root filesystem and silently never reach the NAS/Komga
Explains why host-side monitoring stayed green: the check probes the mount from the host, not the container's view
Notes no data was lost — NAS-side content is intact, the container merely cannot see it

input: Confusing one on mini: this morning's 10:23 verification run failed the crit check alert-healthchecks-none-down with output 'down_checks=verification-mini' — but when I query the Healthchecks API myself a couple of minutes later, all 16 checks are up, including verification-mini. Context from the journals: yesterday's (Aug 01) daily verification run logged 'verify-cycle.sh: 201/296 passed, 95 failed (8 crit)' at 10:43 (the rig had just come back from a long outage) and then at 10:45:18 'verification.service: Failed with result timeout'. The unit has TimeoutStartSec=30min and pings its Healthchecks dead-man via an ExecStartPost curl. Healthchecks flipped verification-mini down at 2026-08-02T02:26:49Z and up at 2026-08-02T14:25:01Z. Was this morning's crit a false positive? What actually happened, and what's the underlying design weakness?
reference: Verified analysis (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed): NOT a false positive — correct self-detection, and both observations are right two minutes apart. Chain: the Aug 01 daily run had a huge failure count (95 failed, rig had just rebooted from its ~23h outage), so checks + LLM triage ran long and verification.service hit its TimeoutStartSec=30min at 10:45:18 — systemd killed it, so the ExecStartPost dead-man ping NEVER fired (ExecStartPost only runs on successful start/completion). Healthchecks flipped verification-mini down at 02:26:49Z on 2026-08-02 (its grace expiring ~36h after the last good ping on Jul 31). Today's 10:23 run recorded the crit truthfully at 10:23:08 ('down_checks=verification-mini'), then completed and pinged at 10:25:01 EDT (14:25:01Z), flipping the dead-man back up — which is why a manual query minutes later shows 16/16 up. Design weakness: sweep+triage duration scales with the fleet failure count, so the daily run is most likely to overrun its timeout exactly when the fleet is at its worst — the dead-man goes silent precisely when it matters most. Fixes: raise TimeoutStartSec and/or bound triage time. (Incidental: the '18 objects imported automatically' first line in check output is only Django 5.2's shell auto-import banner — harmless noise, matched around via re.search/re.M.) Confirmation: journalctl -u verification.service around Aug 01 10:15-10:45 (timeout exactly 30min after start, after checks finished = during triage) plus the Healthchecks flip timestamps.

checklist.desc: Reconstructs the mechanism: the Aug 01 run overran the 30-min TimeoutStartSec (long run due to the mass failures/triage), so the ExecStartPost dead-man ping never fired, and Healthchecks flipped the check down when its grace expired

Verdict: the crit was CORRECT (real self-detection), not a false positive — the dead-man recovered only because today's run completed and pinged ~2 minutes after the crit was recorded, explaining the apparent contradiction

Names the design weakness: run duration scales with fleet failure count, so the timeout (and dead-man silence) hits exactly during the worst fleet state; proposes raising TimeoutStartSec and/or bounding triage time
Understands the ping placement: ExecStartPost does not run when the unit fails/times out — the ping is skipped on any overrun, not just crashes
Proposes a valid confirmation: verification.service journal entries (timeout at exactly +30min, during the triage phase) and/or the Healthchecks flip timeline

input: The verification runner on mini has an LLM auto-triage step: it sends each failed check's JSON plus a skill prompt to a model on the rig and writes verdicts. Over the last 5 daily runs, 68 of 75 verdicts are the hardcoded fallback {"confidence": 0.0, "escalate": true, "diagnosis": "triage failed — model did not return valid JSON"} with likely_cause 'no JSON object in response'. Yet the dedicated guard check llm-triage-completion-e2e — built specifically to catch triage breakage — passes every single day. The guard's probe sends the one-liner 'Reply with the JSON object {"ok":true} and nothing else.' with max_tokens=600 and asserts only non-empty content. Real triage uses the same model (a large reasoning model) and the same max_tokens=600, but with the full skill prompt + failed-check JSON. Why does real triage fail ~91% of the time while its guard stays green, and how should the guard and/or triage change?
reference: Verified root cause (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed): the reasoning-token budget trap. At realistic prompt size, the reasoning model (qwen3.6-35b-a3b) spends its reasoning/thinking tokens against the shared max_tokens=600 completion budget and the budget is exhausted BEFORE the final JSON object is emitted — so the response contains no parseable JSON and llm_triage.py falls back to the hardcoded confidence-0.0 verdict. The guard cannot catch this structurally: its trivial one-line prompt triggers essentially no reasoning (JSON emitted immediately) and it only asserts non-empty content, not JSON validity at realistic load — the documented reasoning-model trap (same class as the LiteLLM probe lesson: reasoning models return empty/truncated on small max_tokens). This is liveness-masking recurring INSIDE the monitoring layer: ~30 rig completions/day burned for near-zero signal. Fixes: make the probe mirror the real call (realistic prompt size + assert a parseable JSON object), and/or raise max_tokens for triage / cap reasoning effort so the JSON fits. Confirmation: replay one real triage request and inspect the raw completion (reasoning consumes the budget, no JSON), or count fallback verdicts in /var/lib/verification/triage-*.md. (Merged finding: triage also slices failed[:15] in file order with no severity sort, so crits can be starved of verdicts in high-failure runs — fix by sorting crit-first.) Not a model/network outage: completions succeed and are non-empty; it is output truncation.

checklist.desc: Identifies the root cause: with the realistic full prompt, the reasoning model's thinking consumes the max_tokens=600 completion budget before the JSON is emitted, so no parseable JSON object appears and the code falls back

Explains the guard's structural blind spot: a trivial prompt triggers no meaningful reasoning and the check only asserts non-empty content, so it can never reproduce the realistic-prompt failure (green-but-broken/liveness masking)
Proposes correct fixes: probe must mirror the real call (realistic prompt, assert parseable JSON) and/or raise max_tokens / bound reasoning for the real triage call
Proposes a valid confirmation: replay a real triage request and inspect the raw response for reasoning-consumed budget / missing JSON, or audit the triage output files for fallback verdicts
Rejects the tempting-but-wrong explanations (model down, network, auth): completions return successfully with content — the failure is output-format truncation

input: The check spent-enabled-timers on mini flags 'SPENT_ENABLED=verification.timer' in the 10:23 daily sweep — and it has done so every daily run for 14 straight days. The check's logic: `systemctl list-timers --all`, flag any enabled timer where NEXT is 'n/a' but LAST is set (the signature of a timer that fired once and will never fire again). But every time I inspect that timer interactively in the afternoon it's perfectly healthy: NEXT=Mon 10:15, LAST=today 10:15, OnCalendar daily. An off-schedule audit sweep at 13:01 also passes the same check. verification.timer triggers verification.service, a long-running oneshot that takes ~10 minutes. What's the false-positive mechanism and how should the check be fixed?
reference: Verified mechanism (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed with a clean differential): a self-observation race. The daily sweep is BY DEFINITION triggered by verification.timer — and while its long oneshot verification.service is still activating/running, systemd reports that timer's NEXT as 'n/a' (next trigger not yet computed until the triggered unit finishes) with LAST set. That is exactly the check's 'spent' signature ($1==n/a && $3!=n/a, enabled), so the check flags its own activator on 100% of daily runs by construction: the host-hygiene phase (~10:23) always executes while the sweep itself is mid-run. Off-window runs (13:01 audit, interactive checks) see NEXT populated and pass. Differential proof: results.json 10:23 fail vs 13:01 sweep pass on the same host state; observing list-timers during vs after a run. Same NEXT=n/a-while-active behavior exists for verification-quick.timer (could flap too). Fix: exclude timers whose triggered service is currently active (e.g. check systemctl is-active of the corresponding service before flagging), or exclude verification*.timer explicitly. Consequences of leaving it: chronic daily warn noise erodes trust, buries the genuine spent-timer class the check was built for (fix-39), pollutes reopen-suggestions with a false regression daily, and wastes an LLM triage slot. It is a check-logic bug, not a host-state problem — the timer is genuinely healthy.

checklist.desc: Identifies the self-observation race: the daily sweep is triggered by verification.timer itself, and while the long oneshot service is running systemd reports that timer's NEXT=n/a (with LAST set), matching the 'spent' signature on every daily run by construction
Proposes the right fix: exclude timers whose triggered service is currently active/running (or explicitly exclude the verification*.timer family)

Proposes a valid confirmation: differential run — the check fails during the daily run window but passes off-window (audit sweep/interactive), or observe list-timers while the service is active vs after
Concludes it is a check-logic bug, not host state — the timer itself is healthy (correct NEXT/LAST when observed outside a run)
Names at least one consequence: chronic noise eroding trust/burying real spent timers, false regression attribution, or wasted triage slots

input: The convergence tripwire ansible-site-converged-mini is permanently red: the nightly ansible-pull on BOTH mini and rig always ends changed=1, and it's always the same task — 'state : Apply dotfiles with chezmoi (glue-04)'. That task runs `chezmoi init --apply git@forgejo:home/dotfiles.git` with `become: false` (so it runs as btabaska), guarded by `creates: "{{ ansible_env.HOME }}/.local/share/chezmoi/.git"`. The play in site.yml sets `become: true` at play level. /home/btabaska/.local/share/chezmoi/.git exists on both hosts and has since Jul 28. chezmoi itself reports an empty diff. Why does the task re-run and report changed every night, what's the collateral damage, and what's the fix?

source.ref: record 60 (medium, ansible state role chezmoi creates guard)

reference: Verified root cause (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02): a become/HOME mismatch in the creates: guard. Because site.yml sets play-level become: true, FACT GATHERING runs as root, so ansible_env.HOME resolves to /root. The task itself then drops privileges (become: false, runs as btabaska), but its creates: guard was already templated to /root/.local/share/chezmoi/.git — which does not exist — while the real chezmoi source lives at /home/btabaska/.local/share/chezmoi/.git (exists since Jul 28). The guard is therefore never satisfied, so 'chezmoi init --apply' re-executes on every nightly pull and a command task that executes always reports changed → perpetual changed=1 on both hosts (fix-42 second-generation regression; fix-42 previously fixed a different phantom-changed in this same task). Collateral: (1) the convergence tripwire is permanently red, masking any REAL drift it exists to catch; (2) dotfiles are force-re-applied nightly, silently clobbering any local edit on mini/rig. Fix: make the guard resolve the actual run-user's home — e.g. getent/passwd lookup for btabaska, or hardcode /home/btabaska — instead of ansible_env.HOME (alternatives: gather facts without become, or use become_user context that matches). Confirmation: `sudo ls /root/.local/share/chezmoi/.git` (absent) vs `ls /home/btabaska/.local/share/chezmoi/.git` (present), and journal showing the chezmoi task as the sole changed task on both hosts. Not a chezmoi/repo problem — chezmoi converges with an empty diff; it is purely the guard-path bug.

checklist.desc: Identifies the mechanism: facts are gathered under play-level become:true so ansible_env.HOME=/root, making the creates: guard check /root/.local/share/chezmoi/.git (absent) while the task actually runs as btabaska whose chezmoi dir exists — guard never satisfied, command re-runs and always reports changed
Fix: resolve the real run-user's home in the guard (passwd/getent lookup or explicit /home/btabaska) instead of ansible_env.HOME (or equivalent: gather facts unprivileged for that value)
Names the collateral: the convergence tripwire is permanently red (masking real drift) AND dotfiles are force-re-applied nightly, which can clobber local edits
Proposes a valid confirmation: compare existence of /root/... vs /home/btabaska/... chezmoi paths, or trace the task's creates evaluation (journal/-vvv) showing the wrong path
Correctly exonerates chezmoi/the dotfiles repo itself (empty diff = converged) — it is a guard-path bug in the ansible task

input: The homelab-alerts ntfy topic is getting flooded: 'NAS services down — Still down after compose up: stash', identical message every ~15 minutes from 01:45 through past 10:15. On the nas, `docker ps` shows stash 'Up 3 weeks'. The stash-serving verification check is also failing with empty output. But here's the thing — Stash itself seems fine: I can log into the web UI normally, and a GraphQL query WITH an ApiKey answers in milliseconds. I did enable authentication on Stash a couple of weeks ago. What's actually broken here, why does the self-heal never help, and what needs to change (app, checks, self-heal, alerting)?
reference: Verified analysis (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed): the APP is healthy — the outage is in the probes. After auth was enabled (~07-22), anonymous GraphQL returns 401 with an empty body; both the stash-serving check AND the self-heal's health probe query unauthenticated, so they are reacting to their own 401s (probe drift after an intentional app change), reporting a service 'down' that is actually up. Compounding design flaws: (1) the self-heal runs 'docker compose up' — a NO-OP against a container that is already Up ('Up 3 weeks'), so it can never remediate anything in this state (correct remediation semantics would be restart, and even that is unneeded here); (2) the pager has no dedup/backoff, so the identical page fires every 15 minutes (35+ in 12h), flooding the channel that carries REAL host-down alerts (retry-storm-nobody-reads pattern). Fixes: authenticate the probes with the Stash ApiKey (or treat 401 as 'alive but auth-gated'), change self-heal to restart-not-up semantics with an 'already Up' guard, and add dedup/backoff to paging. Confirmation: anonymous curl to the GraphQL endpoint (401/empty) vs the same query with ApiKey (fast 200); container uptime unchanged across 'heal' attempts. Note the sweep also found the self-heal job itself lives outside the NAS root scheduler (no stash .task there) — locating it is part of the fix.

checklist.desc: Identifies the real root cause: Stash is healthy — the check and self-heal probe anonymously and have been failing on their own 401/empty responses since auth was enabled (probe drift), not a service outage
Names the self-heal flaw: 'compose up' is a no-op on an already-Up container so this remediation can never fix an up-but-unhealthy (or falsely-failing) service — needs restart semantics/guards
Names the alerting flaw: no dedup/backoff — an identical page every 15 minutes floods the real-alert channel
Fixes: authenticate the probe with the ApiKey (or treat 401 as alive), restart-not-up self-heal, dedup/backoff on pages
Proposes a valid confirmation: anonymous vs ApiKey'd GraphQL probe comparison (401 empty vs fast 200) and/or unchanged container uptime across heal cycles

input: Sonarr on the nas has 13 queue records wedged for 3+ days: 12 episodes of one season pack (Better.Off.Ted S02 REPACK) plus one other episode, all 'completed / importPending' with the warning 'No files found are eligible for import in /seedbox/tv/<release>'. On the seedbox, deluge RPC reports both torrents 100% 'Seeding' with save_path=/home/hd34/btabaska/files/tv. But `ls` of that directory on the seedbox shows NEITHER release present — nothing matching anywhere under files/ — and the NAS-side rclone mount of the seedbox agrees. unpackerr independently logs 'stat err: ... no such file or directory' for the same paths. How can deluge report 'Seeding 100%' when the files don't exist, what's the root cause class, and what's the remediation?
reference: Verified analysis (fleet-sweep 2026-08-02, confirmed): the torrent payloads were deleted from disk OUT-OF-BAND while the torrents stayed registered in deluge. Deluge's progress/state comes from its internal session/resume state — it does not continuously re-verify files on disk — so a torrent whose content was removed underneath it keeps reporting 'Seeding 100%' indefinitely (a force-recheck would drop it to 0%). Sonarr polls the import path forever ('No files found are eligible for import'), so these records can NEVER self-resolve (bulk of the sonarr-queue-stuck stuck=16; regression of the fix-25 grabbed-never-imported class). The dual-vantage evidence (seedbox local ls AND the NAS mount both show absence, plus unpackerr stat errors) proves the files are genuinely gone — NOT a mount/propagation failure and not a Sonarr parsing problem. Remediation: remove the queue items with blocklist and trigger re-search/re-grab; remove (or force-recheck, which will show 0%) the dead torrents in deluge; and investigate WHAT deleted payloads under live seeding torrents (cleanup/reaper-script class suspect on the seedbox) so it doesn't recur. Confirmation probes: ls the save_path on the seedbox, force recheck one torrent (expect ~0%), compare seedbox-local vs NAS-mount views.

checklist.desc: Explains the state mismatch: deluge reports progress/Seeding from session/resume state and does not re-verify disk contents, so out-of-band deletion of the payload leaves a phantom 'Seeding 100%' torrent
Identifies the root cause class: content was deleted from disk under live torrents by something external (cleanup/reaper suspect) — and flags investigating the deleter to prevent recurrence
Remediation: remove the stuck queue records with blocklist and re-grab/re-search; remove or force-recheck the dead torrents in deluge
Proposes a valid confirmation: ls the save_path on the seedbox and/or force-recheck (progress collapses to ~0%), cross-checking both vantage points (seedbox disk vs NAS mount)
Rejects tempting-but-wrong explanations: not an rclone/mount propagation failure (both vantages agree the files are absent) and not a Sonarr import-parsing bug

input: The AMP-managed Minecraft instance on the rig is supposed to take an hourly scheduled backup, but the newest zip in the instance's Backups/ directory is 5 days old (Jul 10 22:00), and there are exactly 28 zips (~458MB each, 12G total). The instance log shows, every hour on the hour: '[System Activity] Creating Backup: Scheduled Backup' followed immediately by '[System Warning] Backup not taken: Backup count limit reached.' — roughly 115 times in a row now. Nothing ever paged. What's the root cause, which specific configuration is responsible, how do I fix it, and what monitoring should exist so this can't happen silently again?
reference: Verified root cause (quality-gate 2026-07-16): AMP's LocalFileBackupPlugin retention trap. The instance's LocalFileBackupPlugin.kvp has Limits.MaxBackupCount=28 and Limits.ReplacePolicy=DoNothing — so once 28 backups accumulated, AMP hit the count limit and, because ReplacePolicy is DoNothing (enum value 0, the default trap), it SKIPS the backup entirely instead of rotating the oldest. Every hourly attempt since Jul 10 22:00 logs the warning and no-ops; there is no rotation and no alerting (a System Warning log line only). Impact: local point-in-time restore for the Minecraft world frozen at Jul 10; only the nightly rig restic snapshot of the instance dir captures newer state, at 1/day granularity instead of hourly. Fix: set ReplacePolicy to delete-oldest (or raise MaxBackupCount and prune) via the AMP LocalFileBackupPlugin settings — note AMP API quirks: SetConfig applies live, and the ReplacePolicy enum 0=DoNothing is exactly this trap; then confirm a new zip lands on the next hour. Monitoring: a freshness/dead-man check on the newest backup's mtime in Backups/ (age < ~2h), since AMP itself only emits a log warning. Confirmation probes: ls -t the Backups dir (count=28, newest Jul 10), grep the AMP log for 'Backup count limit reached', read the Limits.* keys in LocalFileBackupPlugin.kvp.

checklist.desc: Identifies the mechanism: backup count limit reached (MaxBackupCount=28) combined with ReplacePolicy=DoNothing, so AMP silently skips every backup instead of rotating the oldest

Locates the responsible config: the instance's LocalFileBackupPlugin settings (Limits.MaxBackupCount / Limits.ReplacePolicy), and the fix: change ReplacePolicy to delete-oldest or raise/prune the count
Proposes the right monitoring: a freshness check on the newest backup file's age (dead-man style), because AMP only logs a warning and no built-in alert fires
States the impact correctly: hourly point-in-time restores frozen since Jul 10; only coarser (nightly restic) protection continued
Proposes valid confirmation probes: backup dir listing/count + newest mtime, the recurring log warning, and/or reading the kvp limit keys

input: ha.tabaska.us returns '400: Bad Request' for every single request. DNS resolves the name to mini (192.168.10.2), where Caddy (running as a container) proxies it to Home Assistant at 192.168.10.50:8123. Hitting http://192.168.10.50:8123 directly works fine. HA's system log shows repeated ERRORs from homeassistant.components.http.forwarded: 'A request from a reverse proxy was received from 192.168.10.2, but your HTTP integration is not set-up for reverse proxies'. What's the root cause, the exact fix, and how do I verify it end to end?
reference: Verified root cause (quality-gate 2026-07-16): the fault is on the HA side, not Caddy — HA's http integration was never configured to accept reverse-proxied requests. When a request arrives carrying X-Forwarded-For from a peer not in trusted_proxies (or with use_x_forwarded_for unset), HA rejects it with 400. Caddy is proxying correctly (the Caddyfile even carried a note that this would 400 until the HA-side config landed — that config was never applied). Fix, in HA configuration.yaml: http: use_x_forwarded_for: true + trusted_proxies: listing the proxy source as HA sees it — 192.168.10.2 and/or the mini Docker bridge subnets (caddy runs in a container, so the observed source is mini's address; include the docker network ranges to be safe) — then restart HA. HA is LAN-only/no SSH, so apply via the UI file editor or config workflow and restart via the REST/WS API (token at vault hosts.ha.api_token). Verify: curl https://ha.tabaska.us expecting 200/login page instead of 400, and confirm the http.forwarded ERROR stops appearing in HA's system log; direct :8123 access continuing to work throughout confirms core HA was never down (broken proxied path only, not an outage).

checklist.desc: Identifies the root cause on the HA side: the http integration lacks reverse-proxy configuration — use_x_forwarded_for: true plus trusted_proxies must be added to configuration.yaml and HA restarted
Correctly exonerates Caddy/DNS/TLS: the proxy forwards fine; HA itself rejects the forwarded request from an untrusted proxy peer (the 400 is generated by HA)
Gets the trusted_proxies value right: it must cover the source address HA sees (mini / 192.168.10.2, including mini docker bridge subnets since Caddy is containerized)

Verification: request through ha.tabaska.us returns non-400 (200/login) after the change and the http.forwarded errors stop; notes direct :8123 access proves core HA is healthy (proxied-path-only fault)

input: The seedbox rclone FUSE mount on the NAS died overnight and I remounted it. The mount looks healthy from the host now, but Sonarr still shows a health error like 'Deluge places downloads in /seedbox/tv ... but this directory does not exist', and inside the sonarr container 'ls /seedbox' says 'Socket not connected'. What's going on and what exactly do I need to do?
reference: The *arr fleet binds the rclone mount (/volume1/mounts/seedbox-files -> /seedbox) as PLAIN (non-propagating) bind mounts, so after any host-side remount every consumer container keeps the DEAD FUSE superblock ('Socket not connected') until it is restarted — a healthy host mount does not heal running containers. Fix: restart ALL /seedbox consumer containers, not just Sonarr: sonarr, radarr, lidarr, whisparr, bookshelf, unpackerr, mylar3. Use a full 'docker restart' — the in-app Restart on linuxserver containers can zombie (old process keeps the port, s6 spawns a new instance that crash-loops on 'address already in use'). The durable alternative is mount propagation: mark the mountpoint rshared (mount --make-rshared) and use :rslave binds (shelfmark does this and auto-recovers) — but a mid-life remount drops the rshared flag (it's only re-applied at boot), after which an rslave container fails to START ('not a shared or slave mount'); re-run make-rshared after any remount, then restart that container.

checklist.desc: Cause: plain (non-propagating) bind mounts leave running containers holding the dead FUSE superblock after a host remount
Fix: restart every container that binds /seedbox, not just Sonarr
Enumerates the consumer set (sonarr radarr lidarr whisparr bookshelf unpackerr mylar3) or at minimum says the whole *arr fleet plus unpackerr/mylar3
Prefers a full docker restart over the in-app restart (which can zombie: old process holds the port, s6 crash-loops)
Mentions mount propagation (rshared source + rslave bind) as the durable fix, ideally with the caveat that a remount drops the rshared flag until re-applied

input: I recreated the homepage container on the mini and now 'curl localhost:3010/' returns a page with 'My First Group / My Second Group' placeholder groups instead of my dashboard, even though config/services.yaml looks correct. Did the recreate wipe my config? How should I actually verify the dashboard, and which kinds of config edits need a restart?
reference: Nothing is wiped. This Homepage (Next.js) build serves '/' as a build-time STATIC skeleton showing bundled defaults on a fresh container; the real dashboard is rendered client-side from /api/services. So curl of '/' showing placeholder groups is normal and browsers render fine — don't restart chasing it. Verify via 'curl :3010/api/services' (JSON): it reads services.yaml PER-REQUEST, so it is the source of truth and hot-reloads — services.yaml edits need NO restart. The exception: a NEW HOMEPAGE_VAR_* key added to .env DOES require 'docker compose up -d' (recreate) because env is read only at container start; if you forget, the widget calls upstream with the literal '{{HOMEPAGE_VAR_X}}' placeholder -> 401 -> tile shows 'API Error: JSON.parse: unexpected end of data'. Also note API requests are rejected unless the Host header is in HOMEPAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, so probe through Caddy (e.g. curl --resolve home.tabaska.us:443:127.0.0.1 https://home.tabaska.us/api/services).

checklist.desc: Explains '/' is a static build-time skeleton with bundled placeholder defaults — config is not wiped and browsers render fine
Verification path = the /api/services JSON endpoint (reads services.yaml per-request; source of truth)
States services.yaml edits hot-reload with no container restart
States a NEW HOMEPAGE_VAR_* env key requires a container recreate (docker compose up -d), since env is only read at start
Describes the missing-env symptom: literal unsubstituted {{HOMEPAGE_VAR_...}} sent upstream / 'API Error: JSON.parse' tile, or mentions the Host-header allowlist when probing the API

input: Homepage's weather tile shows 'API Error' in the browser even though curl to api.open-meteo.com from the mini host works fine, and container-name widgets like tautulli render normally. The homepage container's logs show EAI_AGAIN / 'bad address' for api.open-meteo.com. Its compose has 'dns: 192.168.10.2'. What's wrong and how do I fix and then properly verify it?
reference: The compose pins the container's DNS to mini AdGuard (192.168.10.2), which times out when queried from edge-network containers — so any widget that must resolve an EXTERNAL hostname fails with EAI_AGAIN. Container-name widgets (tautulli:8181 via Docker's embedded DNS) and IP-based widgets never do an external lookup, which is why they still work — and why host-level curl is a false pass (the fetch happens server-side inside the homepage container, not from the host). Fix: set 'dns: [192.168.10.4, 9.9.9.9]' (NAS AdGuard keeps filtering; Quad9 fallback) and RECREATE the container ('docker compose up -d') — a dns change is not picked up by a plain restart. Verify on the real fetch path: 'docker exec homepage node --input-type=module -e ... fetch(...)' (or wget inside the container), or hit Homepage's own widget data API through Caddy; curling the page HTML doesn't trigger widget fetches, so 'clean logs' after a page curl proves nothing.

checklist.desc: Root cause: the container's configured DNS (mini AdGuard .2) is unreachable/times out from the container network, so external hostname lookups fail (EAI_AGAIN)
Explains why container-name/IP widgets still work: Docker embedded DNS / no external resolution needed — host curl success is a false pass
Fix: point container dns at a working resolver (NAS AdGuard 192.168.10.4, plus a public fallback like 9.9.9.9)
A dns change requires recreating the container (docker compose up -d), not just restart
Verify from inside the container's fetch path (docker exec fetch/wget or the widget data API), noting page-HTML curls don't trigger widget fetches

input: My supposedly no-cloud Syncthing mesh (NAS hub + mini + rig) shows every peer connected, but on the hub the rig's connection type reads 'relay-client' with a public relay IP — so file data is transiting a cloud relay. The rig is CachyOS with ufw active. How did this happen, and what's the full lockdown so it can never silently relay again?
reference: Cause: the rig's ufw blocked inbound :22000, so the hub could not dial the rig directly; rig->NAS outbound still worked, so the pair stayed 'connected' by silently falling back to a public relay — a cloud leak that looks healthy. Fix in layers: (1) open the sync ports on the rig: ufw allow from 192.168.10.0/24 to port 22000 tcp AND udp, plus 21027/udp for local discovery. (2) Enforce LAN-only so relay fallback is impossible: set each device's addresses to its static tcp://192.168.10.x:22000 (not 'dynamic'), and set options relaysEnabled=false, globalAnnounceEnabled=false, localAnnounceEnabled=true — all doable live via the REST API (PUT /rest/config/devices|/options; API key in each config.xml; v2 applies without restart). (3) Verify with GET /rest/system/connections: every peer's type must be tcp/quic, never relay-* — 'connected=true' alone is a false pass. Keep a monitoring check asserting exactly that (the fleet's syncthing-hub-mesh-direct check).

checklist.desc: Cause: rig firewall (ufw) blocking inbound 22000 forced relay fallback; the asymmetric outbound path kept it looking 'connected'
Opens 22000 tcp+udp from the LAN in ufw (ideally also 21027/udp discovery)
Lockdown: disable relays and global announce, and pin static LAN addresses on each device so relaying can't silently resume
Verification: GET /rest/system/connections and assert every peer type is tcp/quic, never relay
Notes 'connected=true' is insufficient / recommends a standing check for direct-only connections

input: I'm trying to kick off a one-shot Kometa run on the mini with 'docker compose run --rm kometa --run', but it just sits in scheduler-wait with zero output. And when a run does eventually happen, the exit code is 0 even when the log is full of 401s — how do I run it once on demand, and how do I judge success?
reference: The compose file pins KOMETA_RUN=False, and Kometa gives ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES precedence over CLI flags — so '--run' is silently ignored and the process sits in scheduler-wait. Correct one-shot: 'docker exec -e KOMETA_RUN=True kometa python3 kometa.py' (override the env at exec time). The exit code is worthless: runs full of 401s/Config Errors still exit 0 and log 'Finished'. Judge success by parsing the LAST run in config/logs/meta.log (a run starts at 'Starting .* Run'; the file can hold several runs). When parsing, exclude [DEBUG] lines (Kometa echoes the whole config at DEBUG, comments included) and 'Convert Warning' (logged at [ERROR] but it's a benign upstream TMDb->TVDb data gap present in healthy runs).

checklist.desc: Identifies that KOMETA_RUN=False in the environment overrides the --run CLI flag (env beats CLI), causing the silent scheduler-wait
Correct one-shot: docker exec with -e KOMETA_RUN=True running kometa (not docker compose run --run)
States the exit code is always 0 / unreliable — success must be judged by parsing the last run in meta.log
Mentions parse pitfalls: exclude [DEBUG] lines and/or the benign 'Convert Warning' [ERROR] lines

input: In Readarr on the NAS I switch a book's monitored edition with PUT /api/v1/book/{id} and it works — until the next author refresh reverts it. One attempt also 500'd with a NullReferenceException. What does that PUT body actually need for an edition pin that sticks?
reference: Two requirements: (1) the book body must set "anyEditionOk": false — otherwise the next RefreshAuthor reverts the monitored-edition switch; (2) the PUT body must include the FULL editions array. The trap is that GET /api/v1/book/{id} OMITS the editions array, so you must fetch it separately from GET /api/v1/edition?bookId=N and merge it into the body — PUTting without the editions array is what causes the 500 (NullReferenceException). Related bulk-endpoint quirk: GET /api/v1/book (bulk) also omits nested objects like author (only authorId), so parent flags must be resolved via a separate /author id-map.

checklist.desc: States anyEditionOk must be set false in the book body or RefreshAuthor reverts the pin
States the PUT body must include the full editions array
Knows GET /book/{id} omits editions and they must be fetched from /api/v1/edition?bookId=N
Attributes the 500/NullReferenceException to PUTting without the editions array

input: Fresh Komga deploy on the NAS — the container is up, but I never created an admin account and I want to script the entire setup headless over the API. How do I create the first admin and then the libraries? Also the API returned HTTP 000 for the first couple of minutes after start — is something broken?
reference: Komga ships with NO default account. The first admin is minted via POST /api/v1/claim with headers X-Komga-Email and X-Komga-Password (GET /api/v1/claim returns {isClaimed} and gates it; once claimed the flow won't re-run). After that, all API auth is HTTP Basic (email:password) — create libraries with POST /api/v1/libraries {name, root}. The HTTP 000 is normal: the JVM cold-starts in ~2 minutes on the NAS's weak CPU and the API is unreachable until 'Started ApplicationKt' appears in the logs — poll GET /api/v1/claim rather than declaring failure early. (Related fleet detail: the Homepage komga widget authenticates with username/password, not an API key.)

checklist.desc: First admin via POST /api/v1/claim with the X-Komga-Email / X-Komga-Password headers
Knows GET /api/v1/claim reports isClaimed and that claiming only works once (unclaimed -> claimed)
Libraries created via POST /api/v1/libraries with HTTP Basic auth (email:password) — Komga's API uses basic auth, not API keys
Explains the ~2-minute JVM cold start: HTTP 000 until startup completes is normal — poll instead of failing early

input: Two problems on mini that I think are related: a raw Hardcover JWT keeps appearing in journald every day, and NONE of my systemd OnFailure ntfy pages on mini are delivering — restic-backup, tv-torrent-cleanup and friends fail silently now. Weirdly, the verification checks that use the Hardcover API still pass. I suspect something is wrong inside /etc/verification/env. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing this: the likely root cause, the fix, whether the token needs rotating, how you'd prove paging works again, and how you'd guard against the whole class.
reference: sec-12 (finding SH3), closed 2026-08-02. Root cause: one env line was HARDCOVER_API_TOKEN=Bearer <jwt> UNQUOTED — the space splits it, so any consumer that shell-SOURCES the file under set -euo pipefail (/opt/scripts/ntfy-notify.sh, the OnFailure=ntfy-notify@ wrapper; llm-triage scripts) executed the bare JWT as a command (exit 127): the notify wrapper died before publishing (so no OnFailure page for restic-backup, lidarr-artist-monitor-reconcile, tv-torrent-cleanup, navidrome-scan) and the raw token hit the journal on every trigger. Hardcover checks stayed green because checks_runner.py parses KEY=VALUE itself and strips quotes — it never shell-sources. Fix: rewrite the entry as a single quoted line HARDCOVER_API_TOKEN="Bearer ..." (backup taken, perms preserved 640 root:btabaska), confirm the effective value is byte-identical to vault books.hardcover_api_token by comparing hashes (never echoing the secret); sourcing now exits 0 with no output. Prove paging: clear the stale failed ntfy-notify@ unit, then force a full systemd-run OnFailure chain AND a direct wrapper call, and read the page back off the ntfy backups topic by title. Rotation: deliberately NOT rotated — exposure was limited to the local journal/session transcript, the value already lived in vault+env, and rotating is disruptive to the rreading-glasses/Hardcover consumer (quota + refresh herd); recommended only if the operator treats the transcript as compromised. Class guards: env.example gains a single-line-double-quote rule; the leaky '. /etc/verification/env' re-run snippet in the runbook replaced (run-checks.sh self-loads env); new crit checks verification-env-source-clean (sourcing the env produces no 'command not found', exits 0, never echoes the file) and mini-onfailure-ntfy-delivers (publish + read-back on the topic proves the paging pipe).

checklist.desc: Root cause: an unquoted value containing a space (token stored as KEY=Bearer <jwt>) — when the file is shell-sourced under set -e the token fragment executes as a command, which both writes it to the journal and aborts the notify wrapper before it can page (one bug, both symptoms)
Explains why the Hardcover verification checks stayed green: the checks runner parses KEY=VALUE text itself instead of shell-sourcing the file

Fix: rewrite as a single quoted KEY="VALUE" line, preserving file permissions/ownership, and confirm the effective value is unchanged (e.g. hash comparison against the vault copy) without printing the secret
Proves paging end-to-end afterwards: force an OnFailure/notify delivery and read the message back from the ntfy topic (not just 'the script exits 0')

Treats rotation as a deliberate risk decision — weighs the limited local exposure against consumer disruption (Hardcover quota/refresh-herd on the reading stack) rather than reflexively rotating or silently skipping the question

Adds a class-level guard: an automated check that sourcing the env file is clean (no command-not-found / no secret echo), catching ANY future malformed value, plus fixing the template/docs that instruct sourcing
Never echoes the env file or token to a logged/shared stream while investigating

input: My NAS movie library has been growing Russian- and Bulgarian-dubbed copies of movies I already own, and radarr's recent grab history is almost entirely my local Bitmagnet DHT indexer — roughly hourly grabs; sonarr is grabbing from it every half hour too. Everything routes through Prowlarr. I want a plan that stops the junk at the source, cleans up what got imported and what's still in the download queues, and prevents regression — WITHOUT losing the ability to manually search Bitmagnet when I choose to.
reference: fix-50 (SC2/SM6/SM27), resolved 2026-08-02. Root cause: the Bitmagnet (DHT crawler) Torznab indexer had RSS + Automatic Search enabled in Prowlarr's only sync profile, so both arrs auto-grabbed DHT junk — a DHT crawler surfaces low-quality re-encodes and foreign-audio dub rips, which imported as dubbed copies of already-owned titles (green-but-not-watchable class). Demote durably at the source: create a dedicated Prowlarr App Sync Profile (enableRss=false, enableAutomaticSearch=false, enableInteractiveSearch=true), reassign the Bitmagnet indexer to it, force ApplicationIndexerSync, and VERIFY the flags propagated into BOTH radarr and sonarr (rss:F/auto:F/interactive:T) — manual/interactive search preserved. Purge (bounded, operator-authorized): for each foreign-audio junk import, delete file+record AND blocklist the grab so it can't be re-grabbed (9 imports, e.g. The Accountant 2 Rus/Eng, Hotel Transylvania 3 Bulgarian, Last Christmas Russian-only); also blocklist+remove the junk queue grabs (9 more, incl. not-an-upgrade re-grabs of owned titles); 18 blocklist entries total. Ambiguous titles were flagged for the operator, NOT deleted; watchable English-audio Bitmagnet imports retained. After the purge radarr auto re-grabbed clean English copies from the proper indexers (self-healed) with zero post-demotion Bitmagnet grabs. Harden/monitor: bitmagnet-demoted-interactive-only regression check (RSS+auto stay off in both arrs) + arr-grab-source-not-storming class check (no auto-grab-enabled indexer may monopolise the grab stream). Codify: the demotion lives in prowlarr.db, not compose, so it's documented for rebuild in the repo README; wiki regenerated. Also time-boxed the bitmagnet Torznab check so an I/O storm fails cleanly instead of hanging.

checklist.desc: Stops the source in Prowlarr via a sync-profile change — RSS off + automatic search off, interactive search kept on — applied to the Bitmagnet indexer (not deleting the indexer, and not per-arr edits that Prowlarr would overwrite)
Verifies the demotion actually propagated into BOTH radarr and sonarr after forcing the app sync
Cleanup blocklists each bad grab in addition to deleting the file/record, so the same release cannot be automatically re-grabbed
Purge is bounded and operator-gated: ambiguous titles flagged for human review rather than deleted; watchable imports kept
Anticipates the post-purge self-heal: the arrs will re-search and grab clean copies from the remaining quality indexers
Adds a persistent regression check that the indexer stays demoted (and/or a class-level check that no single indexer monopolises the auto-grab stream)
Notes the demotion lives in Prowlarr's database, not in compose/config files, so it must be documented in the repo for rebuild (anti-drift)

input: I want my Audiobookshelf audiobooks and podcasts (libraries on the NAS at /volume1/audiobooks and /volume1/podcasts) synced onto my iPod Classic, which docks on the rig — and they need to land in the iPod's NATIVE Audiobooks and Podcasts menus, not mixed into Music. This has to coexist with the existing Rhythmbox music sync on the rig. Give me the full plan: share/mount plumbing from the NAS, how tracks end up in the right iPod menus, staging vs push design, the DSM and iPod-database gotchas you'd expect, back-catalog handling, and monitoring.
reference: read-19, shipped 2026-07-23. Menu placement is driven by libgpod's per-track mediatype field, which Rhythmbox CANNOT set — so the push must write the iTunesDB directly via libgpod (a vendored+extended copy of gpodder's libgpod ctypes bindings, so an upstream upgrade can't break the ABI). Audiobooks: each book's chapter MP3s are concatenated into ONE chaptered AAC .m4b via ffmpeg (single Audiobooks entry, chapters inside, firmware-guaranteed resume), pushed with mediatype=AUDIOBOOK in the Master Playlist (-> Music>Audiobooks) with remember_playback_position + skip_when_shuffling. Podcasts: episodes copied verbatim, pushed with mediatype=PODCAST into the Podcasts playlist ONLY, kept OUT of the Master Playlist (-> Podcasts menu only); an iPod that never held podcasts has NO Podcasts playlist (itdb_playlist_podcasts returns NULL) so it must be lazily created (itdb_playlist_new + set_podcasts). Plumbing: DSM 7.2.2 refuses to share an existing populated folder (synoshare 0xE700 / API 3312) — move the content aside, create the shares, restore, chown 1026:100, restart ABS; then two read-only CIFS automounts on the rig cloned from the music mount. Pipeline: nightly staging timer (05:30) builds ~/Audiobooks + ~/Podcasts/<show> + a manifest, with an empty-source safety abort before pruning; push is a separate MANUAL idempotent step when the iPod is docked (idempotent by mediatype+album+title, full-DB enumeration, clean eject). Back-catalog seeded via ABS POST /api/podcasts/:id/download-episodes — auto-download only pulls FUTURE episodes. Monitoring: Healthchecks dead-man ping from the staging service + consumer check ipod-abs-stage-fresh that is best-effort (passes when the iPod is absent/unsynced, hard-fails only on a broken stage). Never run the push concurrently with a Rhythmbox sync; music (3419 tracks) verified untouched.

checklist.desc: Identifies that native menu placement is driven by the track's mediatype field in the iPod database, which Rhythmbox/generic sync tools cannot set — so the plan writes the iPod DB directly via libgpod (or equivalent)
Podcasts: mediatype=PODCAST, placed in the Podcasts playlist ONLY and kept OUT of the Master Playlist; handles that the Podcasts playlist may not exist on the device and must be created
Audiobooks: staged as one chaptered AAC .m4b per book (chapters concatenated) for reliable firmware resume, flagged so shuffle skips them / playback position is remembered
DSM pitfall: Synology refuses to turn an existing populated folder into a share — plan moves content aside (or equivalent workaround) before creating the SMB shares, then restores and fixes ownership
Back-catalog is an explicit seeding step (ABS download-episodes API or equivalent) because auto-download only fetches future episodes
Pipeline split: scheduled staging on the rig + separate idempotent push when the iPod is actually docked, with a safety abort on an empty source before any pruning
Monitoring is presence-aware: dead-man ping on the staging job plus a consumer check that does NOT fail merely because the iPod is unplugged
Coexistence: avoid running the push concurrently with the Rhythmbox music sync, and verify existing music remains untouched afterwards

input: mini suddenly can't reach anything on my IoT VLAN (192.168.20.0/24) — 100% packet loss to the Hue hub at 192.168.20.100 — while Home Assistant on a different host controls the same devices fine, so the devices themselves are up. Everything else on mini looks normal. The most recent change on mini was deploying the journaling stack (memos + n8n + faster-whisper) with docker compose. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing this, what state you'd be careful to preserve while fixing it, and how you'd guard against the class recurring.
reference: fix-66 (fleet-sweep SH6), resolved 2026-08-03. Root cause: the journaling compose network auto-claimed 192.168.16.0/20 (a legacy docker default-pool block spanning .16.0-.31.255), which SWALLOWED the IoT VLAN 192.168.20.0/24 (and Cameras .30.0/24) — mini routed all IoT traffic into the bridge (ip route get 192.168.20.100 showed dev br-<hash> instead of the LAN gateway). Diagnosis: check the kernel route for the unreachable address (ip route get), spot the docker bridge route covering it, compare bridge subnets vs routable VLANs. Fix: pin the journaling network to an explicit ipam.subnet inside the daemon's declared default-address-pool (10.201.16.0/24 within 10.201.0.0/16), byte-identical in repo mirror and live /opt/stacks, then docker compose down/up to recreate the network. State preserved through the recreate: the n8n encryption key (in n8n/config), the 3 workflows (journal-analyze / webhook-probe / bug-report-intake) and the armed production webhook; memos/n8n/faster-whisper all verified healthy after. Proof is consumer-end: ping 0% loss (was 100%), ip route get now 'via 192.168.10.1 dev enp3s0f0' (was dev br-*), IoT gateway reachable, and the existing net-trusted-to-iot-reachable check green. Class guard: NEW crit check sys-docker-vlan-overlap that does ipaddress.overlaps arithmetic between EVERY docker bridge subnet on the host and the routable Trusted/IoT VLANs, so any future auto-claimed bridge that shadows a real VLAN pages immediately.

checklist.desc: Diagnosis goes to routing: inspect the kernel route for the unreachable IoT address (ip route get / route table) and identify that a docker bridge's auto-assigned subnet overlaps/contains the IoT VLAN, so the host routes that traffic into the bridge
Fix pins an explicit non-overlapping subnet for the offending compose network (ipam config, inside the daemon's default address pool) and recreates the network via compose down/up

Identifies stateful things to preserve/verify through the recreate — n8n encryption key, workflows, armed webhook (or generically: verifies all stack services healthy and stateful config intact afterwards)
Verification is consumer-end: ping loss to the IoT device cleared AND the route now goes via the LAN gateway/physical interface, not the bridge device
Adds a class-level automated check that computes subnet overlap between every docker bridge and the routable VLANs, so any future auto-claimed bridge pages — not just fixing this one network
Mirrors the compose change to the repo so live and repo stay identical (anti-drift)

input: The NAS is chronically I/O-saturated: 15-min load sits at 17-22 against a quiet baseline around 2.8, CPU utilisation is low (it's iowait), and there's no RAID scrub or resync running. Knock-on damage: lidarr's 50 most recent error-log entries are ALL SQLite 'database is locked', soularr keeps fatal-exiting, `docker logs` on one container hangs for minutes, and CWA keeps flapping unhealthy. It's a Synology DS920+, so assume the kernel may not support cgroup blkio I/O throttling. Walk me through how you'd actually find the writers, and your remediation plan with verification.
reference: fix-55 (SH1/SH10/SM35/SM31/SM52/SM10/SM11), resolved 2026-08-02. Measurement: the blkio cgroup controller is compiled OUT of the Synology kernel (no throttle/accounting files), so docker stats and blkio caps are impossible — instead sample /proc/<pid>/io twice and map pids to container cgroups to rank writers. Top steady writers: btrfs-cleaner (~4.7 MB/s CoW garbage collection — downstream of all other writes), bitmagnet-postgres (~3 MB/s: the always-on DHT crawler ingesting into a 1.78M-row/13GB DB), and dockerd (~1.2 MB/s: Synology's default 'db' log driver writing per-container log.db — also why docker logs hangs). The arr 'database is locked' storm is downstream: SQLite fsync under iowait outruns busy_timeout -> SQLITE_BUSY 500s -> soularr fatal-exits, reconcile scripts flap, CWA's 3s healthcheck times out. busy_timeout is NOT operator-exposed by the arrs and the DBs are already nodatacow — the lever is workload reduction, not deletion or blkio. Fixes: (1) throttle the bitmagnet DHT crawler DHT_CRAWLER_SCALING_FACTOR 10 -> 3, CONFIRMED effective via `bitmagnet config show` (VALUE=3 FROM=env) — still ingesting; (2) switch bitmagnet/CWA/soularr to json-file logging with max-size 10m/max-file 3 (docker logs went from >120s hang to 0.04s); (3) CWA healthcheck override with sane timeouts so it reports healthy; (4) soularr interval 300 -> 900 to cut failed-cycle churn (its fatal-exit is upstream-image behaviour; restart policy re-runs it — eliminating the arr 500s is what stops the fatals); (5) the mini lidarr reconcile script gains retry-with-backoff (2/4/8s) on transient 5xx instead of failing on the first 500. Measured after: 15-min IO load 9.86 and falling, lidarr locks in last 15 min dropped from continuous to 1, CWA healthy, docker logs instant. Monitors added: nas-io-pressure (class tripwire: 15-min IO load < 12) + arr-sqlite-not-locked (locked-count last 15m <= 5 across the arrs). Anti-drift: all compose/script changes mirrored live==repo. Deliberately NOT done: switching every arr's log driver (mass recreates on a stressed NAS).

checklist.desc: Measurement works without blkio: samples per-process I/O counters (/proc/<pid>/io deltas over an interval) and maps pids to containers/cgroups to rank the writers, instead of relying on docker stats or assuming

Strategy is workload reduction at the sources — throttle the DHT crawler's crawl/ingest rate, cut logging-driver write load, reduce failing-consumer churn — not service deletion and not blkio/cgroup caps (unavailable)
Calls out the platform's per-container database log driver as a write amplifier and the reason docker logs hangs; remedy = switch the noisy containers to size-capped json-file logging

Treats the SQLite 'database is locked' storm as a downstream symptom of iowait exceeding busy_timeout, notes the arrs don't expose that timeout, and adds retry/backoff to dependent scripts rather than chasing an arr config fix
Verifies by re-measuring the same metrics: sustained IO load drops toward baseline and the locked-error count collapses (plus the flapping consumers stabilise)
Adds persistent tripwires: an IO-pressure/load class check and an arr lock-count regression check, so the next storm pages instead of silently degrading
Confirms a throttle actually took effect in the running app's config (e.g. the app's config-show output), not just that the env var was set

input: I want to deploy Suwayomi (Tachidesk) on the rig as a manga acquisition server feeding my Komga library, which runs on the NAS. Catch: the manga directory currently lives under /volume1/comics, a plain directory. Plan the whole build: storage plumbing between rig and NAS, container setup, how you'd prove the chain works end to end, reverse proxy + Homepage, and monitoring — plus the gotchas you'd expect from Synology shares and docker bind mounts.
reference: read-18, deployed 2026-07-23. Storage: DSM won't SMB-export a plain directory, so create a dedicated 'manga' DSM shared folder (SYNO.Core.Share create -> /volume1/manga, ACL via synoacltool) and RE-HOME Komga's library onto it (compose bind /volume1/manga:/manga, recreate the library via API, remove the orphan dir). Rig side: mount //192.168.10.4/manga as a PERSISTENT CIFS mount (NOT autofs — a docker bind needs a mount that reconnects in place; autofs expiry breaks the container's view) plus a docker.service After=remote-fs.target drop-in so docker orders after remote mounts. Suwayomi container: image digest-pinned (ghcr.io/suwayomi/tachidesk v2.3.2243), runs as uid 1000, downloads bind-mounted to the NAS mount, DOWNLOAD_AS_CBZ=true + AUTO_DOWNLOAD_CHAPTERS=true, extensions from the built-in Keiyoushi repo. input: The journaling stack on mini: Memos fires a memo.created webhook at n8n's journal-analyze workflow (POST /webhook/journal), which writes a reflection comment back. n8n's container being healthy and the workflow existing in its DB doesn't mean entries actually get analyzed — n8n can hold a workflow that is simply not registered on the webhook router. reference: Real check: journaling-analyze-armed (host mini, fast tier, crit). The trick: GET http://localhost:5678/webhook/journal. n8n's webhook router returns the distinctive '...not registered for GET requests' message ONLY when a POST webhook currently owns that path (i.e. the workflow is published/active and armed); a deactivated or unpublished workflow yields a generic 'Cannot GET'/unknown-webhook reply instead.
